title: A Cop Stopped an Escaped Killer… and Let Him Go
style: Dillinger flat cartoon-silhouette poster style, cuts locked to the music beat (music re-used from Dillinger); PD US Marshals / BOP photos as evidence inserts
lines: A cop stopped an escaped killer. On camera. They talked for ten minutes. And then... he let him go.
April 5th, 2006. Ball, Louisiana. Officer Carl Bordelon spotted a man running along the railroad tracks.
The man was calm. Friendly. He gave a fake name, said he was just out jogging, and even cracked jokes.
The officer had heard about a prison break nearby. But he had no photo, and no reason to hold him. So he let him walk away.
That man was Richard Lee McNair. A convicted murderer. And this was not his first escape. It was his third.
Rewind to 1987. Minot, North Dakota. McNair, an Air Force sergeant, was caught breaking into a grain elevator. He killed one man, and wounded another.
At the police station, they handcuffed him to a chair. He found a tube of lip balm, greased his wrist, and slipped right out.
He didn't get far that time. But it was a warning of what was coming.
He got life in prison. In 1992, he and two other inmates crawled out through an air vent in the state penitentiary.
He stayed free for nine months, until police finally caught him in Nebraska.
So they sent him somewhere tougher. A high security federal prison in Pollock, Louisiana.
There, McNair had a job. Repairing old, torn mailbags. And day after day, he planned.
He built a hiding pod under a pile of mailbags, with a tube to breathe through. The pallet was moved to a warehouse outside the fence. He cut his way out, and walked away.
Hours later, he met Officer Bordelon on the tracks, and talked his way free. But that was only the beginning.
Within days, he was on the US Marshals' 15 Most Wanted list. About two weeks after the escape, he slipped across the border into Canada.
In British Columbia, police stopped a stolen car. The driver jumped out and ran. Even a police dog couldn't find him.
Then an officer watched America's Most Wanted, and recognized the face. Fingerprints from the car confirmed it. It was McNair.
October 25th, 2007. Campbellton, New Brunswick. A routine traffic stop by the Mounties. Eighteen months on the run, over.
Today he's back behind federal bars, serving life. But one question remains. Investigators believe someone helped him. McNair swears he did it alone.
Genius, or inside help? Tell me in the comments. Then watch ESCAPED number one, the man who broke out with a wooden gun. And follow for more escapes.

notes: Sources: Wikipedia 'Richard Lee McNair'; NBC News 'Through cunning, killer escaped time and again' (2007); Fox News 'Cunning escaped killer is captured in Canada' / 'One of nation's most wanted fugitives captured'; Prairie Public 'McNair Escapes' (Dakota Datebook 2022); CBC 'Mounties capture most-wanted killer in N.B.'; US Marshals release 25 Oct 2007; BOP press release April 2006; Castanet 'U.S. Fugitive in Penticton'; byronchristopher.org on Bordelon. Facts: 17 Nov 1987 Minot grain elevator burglary, killed one man (not named on screen), wounded another; Air Force sergeant at Minot AFB. Early 1988 lip balm slipped handcuffs at Minot police station (sources differ on details). 9 Oct 1992 escaped NDSP Bismarck with two others via ventilation duct, recaptured 5 Jul 1993 Grand Island, Nebraska. Moved to federal custody; USP Pollock. 5 Apr 2006 escaped hidden in a pallet of mailbags (worked repairing mailbags); dashcam encounter with Ball officer Carl Bordelon on railroad tracks the same day. 13 Apr 2006 Marshals 15 Most Wanted; crossed into BC from Blaine WA ~2 weeks later; Penticton: fled on foot from stolen car, dog unit failed; identified via America's Most Wanted + fingerprints. 25 Oct 2007 RCMP traffic stop Campbellton NB; $25,000 reward. Investigators believed outside help; McNair says he acted alone. Do not claim ADX/supermax; Wikipedia lists USP McCreary.
